title: Trade rules are fractured – Australia needs a fallback
gist: About US$11.6 trillion of merchandise trade — 23% of the global total — now runs through the US or China and is exposed to discrimination from one side or the other, with Washington abandoning WTO commitments and Beijing hollowing them out from within. The author argues WTO restoration is a low-probability scenario and that Australia's fallback should be the CPTPP, now roughly 15% of global GDP, plus Cairns Group-style sectoral coalition-building.

themes.theme: The scale of rule-free trade exposure

insights.claim: About US$11.6 trillion of merchandise trade — 23% of the global total — runs through either the United States or China and is therefore exposed to discrimination from one side or the other.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Quantifies the share of world trade now priced with political rather than legal risk — a persistent risk premium for exporters routed through either bloc.
insights.quote: About US$11.6 trillion of merchandise trade – 23% of the global total (Opens in new window) – runs through either the United States or China
insights.locator: About US$11.6 trillion of merchandise trade

insights.claim: US import conditions form a hub-and-spokes arrangement set in Washington and changeable at any time, while China's are formally rules-based but shadowed by coercion — with both powers still participating in WTO processes as though nothing has changed.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Two distinct failure modes — arbitrary discretion versus procedural coercion — require different corporate hedges, not one generic 'trade war' hedge.
insights.quote: US import conditions form a hub-and-spokes arrangement set in Washington, changeable at any time. China’s are formally rules-based but shadowed by coercion.
insights.locator: US import conditions form a hub-and-spokes arrangement

insights.claim: Countries holding free trade agreements with the United States or China — Australia has both — have lost the predictability those agreements were meant to guarantee.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: FTA coverage no longer prices as protection; discount the risk-mitigation value of bilateral trade deals with either superpower.
insights.quote: have lost the predictability those agreements were meant to guarantee
insights.locator: Countries with FTAs with the United States or China

insights.claim: A new 12.5% US tariff on Australian imports, imposed over an alleged failure to ban goods made with forced labour, is the first time Australia has been penalised under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: A first-ever Section 301 action against a close ally sets precedent — allied status is no longer a shield, raising tail risk for other US partners.
insights.quote: 12.5% US tariff on Australian imports over an alleged failure (Opens in new window) to ban goods made with forced labour marks the first time Australia has been penalised under Section 301
insights.locator: The challenges with the United States will persist

insights.claim: Section 301 makes Washington prosecutor, judge and executioner, with carve-outs limited mainly to goods the United States cannot itself produce in volume, leaving contesting parties little prospect of reprieve.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: The exemption logic — only goods the US can't make itself — tells you which import categories are structurally safe from Section 301 action.
insights.quote: Section 301 makes Washington prosecutor, judge and executioner, with carve-outs limited mainly to goods the US cannot itself produce in volume

insights.claim: The 12.5% Australian tariff replaces a universal 10% rate imposed in February after the Supreme Court invalidated Donald Trump's earlier reciprocal tariffs, showing the administration substitutes legal authorities rather than abandoning tariffs when struck down.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Litigation wins against US tariffs deliver at best temporary relief — assume effective tariff levels persist through authority-shopping.
insights.quote: This tariff replaces a universal 10% rate imposed in February after the Supreme Court invalidated Donald Trump's earlier “reciprocal” tariffs.
insights.locator: This tariff replaces a universal 10% rate

insights.claim: Washington has revived a dormant 1930 Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act provision against Canada empowering the president to impose duties of up to 50% on any country judged to be discriminating against US commerce — broad enough to potentially target trade agreements that do not even involve the United States.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: A 50% ceiling authority with extraterritorial reach means third-country trade pacts now carry US retaliation risk — a new variable in any CPTPP or EU deal calculus.
insights.quote: empowering the president to impose duties of up to 50% on any country he judges to be discriminating against US commerce

insights.claim: China has contributed to the impotence of trade rules by exploiting gaps in WTO rules on state subsidies and using macroeconomic policy to artificially expand export supply and suppress import demand.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: China's export surge is treated here as a macro-policy choice, not just competitiveness — implying persistent global deflationary goods pressure and rising trade defence actions.
insights.quote: exploiting gaps in WTO rules on state subsidies and using macroeconomic policy to artificially expand export supply and suppress import demand
insights.locator: China has contributed to the impotence of trade rules

insights.claim: Beijing has repurposed WTO trade remedy tools — anti-dumping and countervailing duty investigations — as instruments of retaliation rather than genuine responses to unfair trade, creating a rules-based façade with immediate deterrent effect.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: The launch of a Chinese anti-dumping probe should be read as a political signal about a pending policy decision, not as a technical trade action.
insights.quote: Beijing has repurposed (Opens in new window) WTO trade remedy tools – anti-dumping and countervailing duty investigations – as instruments of retaliation rather than genuine responses to unfair trade.

insights.claim: Australian wine exports collapsed under Chinese tariffs of up to 218% for three years and still have not fully recovered even though the duties were lifted in 2024.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Coercion inflicts permanent market-share loss beyond the tariff period — the recovery trade after a Chinese ban lift is weaker than headlines suggest.
insights.quote: Australian wine exports collapsed under tariffs of up to 218% for three years and still haven't fully recovered since the duties were lifted in 2024.

insights.claim: The rules-based façade lets Beijing impose rapid costs on governments merely considering action against surges in imports of Chinese goods, chilling policy before it is announced.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Anticipatory deterrence means many trade-defence measures are never proposed — the observed level of protection understates the underlying pressure.
insights.quote: a rules-based façade that still lets Beijing impose rapid costs on governments considering action against surges in imports of Chinese goods
insights.locator: These actions follow WTO procedures on paper

insights.claim: Restoration of the WTO, while worth advocating, is a low-probability scenario because Washington will not easily cede the unilateral flexibility Trump has uncovered and even modest WTO reform is trapped by consensus decision-making.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite a return-to-normal trade scenario; structural fragmentation is the planning base case.
insights.quote: Restoration of the WTO, though worth advocating, is a low-probability scenario.

insights.claim: The CPTPP represents about 15% of global GDP and is Australia's strongest practical platform for rules-based trade, but at eight years old it has been slow to realise its potential.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: CPTPP accession news and EU-CPTPP linkage are the concrete catalysts to watch for a viable third trade bloc forming.
insights.quote: representing about 15% of global GDP and drawing interest from others
insights.locator: The CPTPP is now Australia's strongest practical platform

insights.claim: China's CPTPP membership aspirations are undercut by Beijing's track record of weak domestic reforms, making its accession inconsistent with the bloc's purpose.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Expect continued blocking of China's CPTPP bid — a persistent friction point in Australia-China and CPTPP-member relations.
insights.quote: China’s membership aspirations defy Beijing’s track record of weak domestic reforms
insights.locator: Australia should use it more actively

insights.claim: Australia's response should follow a clear hierarchy — defend the WTO where possible, anchor practical cooperation in the CPTPP, and adapt domestic policy to a more coercive environment — since a middle-sized trade-reliant nation can afford neither nostalgia for a functioning WTO nor resignation to power-based trade.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: A three-tier playbook any small open economy can copy; useful for anticipating similar moves by Canada, Korea, Singapore.
insights.quote: As a middle-sized, trade-reliant nation, Australia can afford neither nostalgia for a functioning WTO nor resignation to power-based trade.
insights.locator: Australia’s response should follow a clear hierarchy

insights.claim: Australia should prepare for more predictable unpredictability by reapplying Cairns Group-style coalition-building sector by sector, accepting that Washington or Beijing may misconstrue any grouping excluding them as a threat, because collective action raises the cost of punitive measures against any one member.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Sectoral coalitions are the emerging defence against coercion — watch for commodity-specific blocs forming outside both superpowers.
insights.quote: acting collectively projects a stronger voice and raises the cost of punitive measures against any one member
insights.locator: Australia should also prepare for more predictable unpredictability

insights.claim: Global supply-chain shocks in recent years have returned industry assistance to the policy mainstream, ending the era in which subsidy was politically off-limits.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Normalised industrial subsidy means sustained fiscal support for domestic manufacturing and critical-input sectors across advanced economies.
insights.quote: Global supply-chain shocks in recent years have returned industry assistance to the policy mainstream.
insights.locator: Global supply-chain shocks in recent years

insights.claim: The lesson from the United States is that trade orthodoxies collapse quickly once a government stops selling the benefits of open markets, so trade policy must be grounded in clear national benefit rather than assuming a domestic free-trade consensus holds indefinitely.
insights.speaker: Stephen Moran
insights.so_what: Political durability of open-market policy is a live risk in every trade-exposed democracy — watch domestic rhetoric as a leading indicator of tariff policy shifts.
insights.quote: One lesson from the United States is that trade orthodoxies collapse quickly once the government stops selling the benefits of open markets.
insights.locator: One lesson from the United States
